relu_triton_kernel.review_basis: Four independently reviewed modules add a total mathematical byte payload with allocated/readable/writable maps and failing ordered accesses. Every active input byte of every pid passes an actual access bind before the pid-zero store gate; a nonzero pid with a missing first active byte fails. All N input words must be readable, while only the first min(N,1024) output words must be writable; the output tail needs no allocation or access permission. Every complete whole-program permutation succeeds on preceding memory and equals the existing byteGrid/independent byteSpec with final tagged LogicalView, typed-grid result, frame and finite-address certificate. Errors retain the mathematical preceding write state, without claiming native faults, poison or fault order. Scalar callbacks are pure and total; nonzero-pid scalar results are not separately evaluated. Zero values outside loaded prefixes merely complete the mathematical container and do not specify original masked no-other load values. Nine existing finite-word profiles and three inherited numerical callbacks are unchanged; native permission/layout/provenance/compiler/host/instruction-interleaving gaps remain open.

remaining_structural_obligations: RELU-A-S1: Native allocation, storage and access permissions. The custom partial interface is a total mathematical byte payload plus explicit allocated/readable/writable maps. Native device allocation, memory validity, access rights, little-endian layout, alignment and provenance are not related to those maps. Full-N input readability and first-tile output writability are selected-domain premises, not host-established facts.

RELU-A-S2: Native source/compiler and error correspondence. Every active input byte of every pid now passes a failing-access bind before the store gate. The nonzero-pid missing-byte theorem distinguishes this from the old total memory-effect projection. This custom interpreter still has no stepwise Python/TTIR/compiler bridge. Deterministic first-unavailable-byte errors and retained partial-write states are mathematical semantics, not native traps, poison, sanitizers or observable fault order. Scalar comparisons/conversions are pure total callbacks; nonzero-pid scalar results are not separately evaluated and no native instruction trace follows. Unloaded entries in loadWords/loadedPrefix are zero placeholders used only to complete the mathematical container; original no-other masked-load values are not specified.

RELU-A-S3: Host-established layout and domains. Logical name distinction, numeric interval separation, B1024, N<2^31 and representable endpoints remain theorem premises. Native empty_like freshness, layouts/strides, shifted/overlapping aliases, other sizes/blocks, launch limits and native zero-grid/error behavior remain open. No allocation or permission is required for the unmodified output tail.

RELU-A-S4: Native instruction interleaving and remaining dtype/module scope. All complete permutations of whole programs are proved in the partial-access model. Programs remain atomic relative to each other; native instruction interleavings and races remain open. The same nine finite-word profiles are refined with no new dtype names. Prior fp64/fp8/error families and host/harness/module/compiler target scope remain required.
